title: Photo required if Not OK vs Photo required, which answers count, HEIC photos
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as a user with "Settings - Service" enabled, on the build under test.
  2. A template checkbox field with both "Photo required" and "Photo required if Not OK" available (seed and turn both on in Settings - Service > Inspection Templates).
  3. You are filling an inspection against that template: open a work order, start the inspection, with "Work order lines - Create & Edit" enabled.
  4. A phone camera that can produce a HEIC photo.
custom_steps:
1. Turn both photo rules on and read the builder's summary sentence.
  2. On the field card footer, find Add Photo beside Add Note; mark Not OK and see the photo target.
  3. Upload a HEIC photo, then a format that cannot be rendered in place.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • This option is separate from "Photo required" (which asks for a photo whatever the response); when both are on the technician is held to the unconditional rule, and the builder's summary sentence says so.
  • The photo target is offered rather than always shown: Add Photo sits in the field card footer beside Add Note and opens the target, or opens on its own the moment a response makes a photo required.
  • Inspection photos accept HEIC as well as JPEG and PNG; where a format cannot be shown in place, the viewer says so and offers the download.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-8181, story SV-9440 (S17 — Require a photo on a Not OK response); Digital Inspections V2 specification, Confluence page 768507905, section S17; read on 22 September 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S17-R7: “The option is separate from "Photo required", which asks for a photo whatever the response. When both are on the unconditional rule is the one the technician is held to, and the summary sentence in the builder says so”
  • S17-R8: “The photo target is offered rather than always shown. Add Photo sits in the field card footer beside Add Note and the target opens on it, or on its own the moment a response makes a photo required, so the technician never has to look for it”
  • S17-R9: “Inspection photographs will accept HEIC as well as JPEG and PNG. A phone camera producing HEIC must not be able to make S17-R3 unsatisfiable. Where the format cannot be rendered in place, the viewer says so and offers the download, as S11-R9 already does for reference files”

Last checked against build v26.36.8-2a64085 on 10/1/2026.

AUTOMATION: READY
